evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The current `manager_restarted` check requires only positive PIDs and differing invocation IDs. A guest reboot also changes both the systemd manager PID and invocation ID, so a reboot can satisfy `manager_restarted` even if the intended manager restart did not occur. The separate `boot_id_changed` check covers the reboot phase and does not bind the manager snapshots to the same boot. Requiring nonempty equal boot IDs on both manager sides is a routine correctness fix.
